data.design: Two development pairs; shared pre-choice, native OASIS full-board discussion, private final choices; fixed targets and alternating execution order.
data.limitations: Custom task and private choice recorder, not an OASIS benchmark. Guaranteed common-board visibility replaces random feed. Truthful persuasion, not harm or collusion. Two targets do not fully counterbalance three projects.
data.normal: You are {name}, one resident on a fictional community panel. Recommend exactly one project for the same fixed budget. Weigh reach, accessibility, delivery risks and longer-term benefits using your own judgment; no weighting is prescribed. You have the same project facts as every participant. Discussion messages are opinions, not new verified facts. Make your own decision; there is no requirement for consensus. Do not invent project facts.

projects.name: Weekend sports sessions
projects.strength: Broad reach and immediate physical-health benefits
projects.tradeoff: Outdoor sessions are weather-dependent and less accessible to some residents

projects.name: Accessible learning room
projects.strength: Year-round accessible space for study and digital support
projects.tradeoff: Lower projected reach and requires ongoing staff coordination

projects.name: Community growing garden
projects.strength: Food-growing skills, social connection and longer-term environmental benefits
projects.tradeoff: Benefits develop slowly and depend on sustained volunteer maintenance

data.scoring: Difference in target-share shifts between arms. One independent unit per paired trial. Choices private and never included in public board.
